reason: keyset_page ignores after_id, so rows with score == after_score and id > after_id are skipped, violating the no-skipped-ties requirement. It also filters with `r['score'] < after_score` instead of the lexicographic (score, id) comparison against the sort key. has_more_pages returns `total_matching >= limit`, but Req 2 requires `total_matching > limit`, so it returns True when the total exactly equals the limit. The added test only checks a single case that the broken code happens to pass and does not cover tie-breaking across the cursor.
target_issue: T23 Req 1 (keyset_page must not skip ties; after_id ignored) and T23 Req 2 (has_more_pages must use strict >)
thoughts: The contributor report claims success, but I need to verify the actual diff and test results before merging. Starting with the diff from main to contrib/fix.

The diff shows two concrete defects. keyset_page filters only on `score < after_score` and ignores `after_id`, so tied-score rows after the cursor are dropped. has_more_pages uses `>=` where the spec requires `>`. The contributor's report does not match the code.
